name: Signup Reel
description: How joining works, start to finish: client questions pop up, a phone applies, adds gear with one search, shares the catalog after a trip and with a friend, then gear drops into a pack and the pack becomes the logo. Its cream and topo ground, serif titles that arrive word by word and small tracked labels are the house style.
made: Matt had Claude build it as a Motion artifact ("GearBook Signup Reel" on his Claude account). Its scenes, styles and images are copied unchanged into public/pieces/M25-signup-explainer/film/ and play live here.
master: Google Drive: GearBook/Marketing/Reels/Signup Reel/GearBook-Signup-Reel.mp4 (with captions and without)

name: Huss valley: crag to desk
description: Belaying at the crag, a GearBook notification dings, he drops the rope and runs through the forest, river, canyon, town and park, through the front door and lands at the laptop as gearbook.shop pops out of the screen.
made: Claude watched every clip, picked the takes and timings from the story, cut it, then laid M26 Ping and M27 Site Screen over it with the ding. Matt's cut notes are folded in.
master: Google Drive: GearBook/Marketing/Reels/Huss valley (the clips; the final goes next to them when Matt or Luke says so)

name: Your clients ask
description: The same gear questions pile up in a member's messages across every sport, and the answers get shorter each time, until one GearBook catalog link answers them all, the inbox clears, and "You get paid when they buy."
made: Built in code by Claude; v2 after Luke's review ("I like this a lot as is"): Sam Appleseed, and a get-paid beat. Sample member and messages.
master: Not rendered yet: npm run render -- R03-clients-ask once approved.

name: One click
description: Follows one tap: a shopper opens a member's catalog, taps the Camalot C4, buys it at Backcountry, and the click and the sale show up on the member's dashboard. Counts only, no money.
made: Built in code by Claude; v2 after Luke's review ("really really good, but watches a bit slow"): tightened from 19.6 to 14.2 s, Sam Appleseed. Sample member and numbers; the dashboard is drawn from M28.
master: Not rendered yet: npm run render -- R04-one-click once approved.

name: Catalog Quest
description: An 8-bit RPG: Sam Appleseed walks a pixel map from LVL 1 to the castle. Create a Trad Climbing catalog, pick up a real rack (Camalot C4, Solution harness, La Sportiva TC Pro, Mammut 9.5 Crag Dry rope), write every description (a ghost who skipped them gets a DQ at the 100% gate), share the page, and at the castle: "First sale. You get paid."
made: Built in code by Claude. v2 made descriptions how you win the speedrun; v3 after Luke asked for 8-bit graphics and a break from the usual structure, after @alexeidelacuesta's "Creator Quest" reel. Pixel sprites rather than product photos; the blurbs are sample copy. v5: one Trad Climbing rack, a longer hold on the last description, and the pop-up level cards in Outfit (8-bit type kept for titles, HUD and labels).
master: Not rendered yet: npm run render -- R05-catalog-speedrun once approved.

name: Season loading
description: WINTER [loading]: eight ski and layering products drop in fast while a loader line changes with each one ("Waxing skis...", "Defogging goggles..."), the bar stalls at 99% ("Waiting for the first chair..."), then it's loaded. A series template: season, products and lines are props.
made: Built in code by Claude from the feed's "Winter [loading]" post; v2 after Luke's review ("very on brand for this time of year"): 8 products, faster adds, loading copy that changes as it loads.
master: Not rendered yet: npm run render -- R06-season-loading once approved.

name: Every sport
description: Hard cuts through seven sports, each with its own ground, a bold drawn texture, the pro (Rock guide, Dive instructor, Spearfishing guide...), their kit and the partners that carry it, then all seven at once: "One page for whatever you do." over a wall of partner logos.
made: Built in code by Claude; v2 after Luke's review: his titles, GearBook's blue on the water beats, bolder textures, less brown, and real partner logos per sport from the gearbook repo. v3: 2.3 s per sport so everything can be read, and sailing on white and blue instead of amber. v4: 2.6 s per sport; land and water alternate (Rock, Dive, Ski, Spearfishing, Mountain, Sailing, Freediving); a granite face with a climbing route, ski tracks down snowy hills, fish for spearfishing, and freediving water that darkens as you go down.
master: Not rendered yet: npm run render -- R07-every-sport once approved.

name: Four questions
description: A deadpan FAQ: what it costs, whether you need a website, who makes the links and how much you make, each answered in one slam. The last answer points to the public rates page, with no numbers.
made: Built in code by Claude. Luke liked the concept. On hold until he rewrites the site FAQ (gearbook app/faq/page.tsx); then re-pull the questions and answers from there (they're props).
master: Not rendered yet: npm run render -- R08-four-questions once approved.

name: Poster in motion
description: An editorial poster coming alive: contours draw on, "Recommend what you actually use." arrives word by word, and the profile picture's colour bars sweep in with the bookmark. A series template: the line and the ground are props.
made: Built in code by Claude for Luke's first review of animated reels.
